title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Analysis situs, third version, June 1986). An 'atelier' is an axiomatic geometric structure. L is a set of basic elements (points or atoms). M is a set of 'figures'. They carry a partial order ≤ on M, an incidence relation x ≪ X (x in L, X in M) and a symmetric relation ∥ ('parallelism', or some kind of separation or apartness). The previous page shows that the figure data can be encoded as (M, ≤, ≪, ∥), with ∥ defined on L, satisfying axioms M0–M4.

The page opens by finishing that sentence. The encoded structures correspond exactly to ateliers satisfying At1–7, AtL1–3 and AtCL(open). So there is an equivalence between the 'set-theoretic' presentation (an atelier with a family of figures) and the 'abstract' presentation (an ordered set M of figures with incidence to L).

Second point. If ∥ is given on M rather than on L, one more axiom is needed. (ML6): X ∥ Y ⟺ for all x, y ∈ L with x ≪ X and y ≪ Y, we have x ∥ y. Thus parallelism of figures is determined elementwise, which makes the M-level relation the one induced from L.

Third point: a variant for polyhedral ateliers, satisfying At1–7, AtL1–3 and AtCL(pol) instead of AtCL(open). The theory is kept, with two changes.
- The definition of the relation X ≫ Y (from p. 29) is modified accordingly.
- An extra condition is imposed on (M, ≤). (ML0 pol): for every X, the down-set X̃ = M_{≤X} is a 'polyhedral ordered set' in the sense of p. 13. That is, two elements Y, Z that have a common upper bound X and a common lower bound T admit an infimum. Equivalently, every interval [T, X] of M has finite infima. Hence it also has finite suprema if it is finite: a finite poset with a top and binary meets is a lattice.

This abstracts the basic property of polyhedral complexes and face posets of polytopes: the intersection of two faces of a cell is a face. The lower bound T plays the role of a non-empty intersection. The purpose is to characterize, purely order-theoretically, which abstract structures (M, ≤, ≪, ∥) come from polyhedral ateliers, as was done for the 'open' case.
errors: No real error. 'Infima in intervals ⇒ suprema' holds only for finite intervals, or under a completeness assumption. Grothendieck hedges with 's'ils sont finis', so the statement is correct as written.

The phrase 'ont des inf finis' is slightly loose. What is meant is that any two elements of the interval [T, X] have a meet in it. The interval has a bottom T, so meets of nonempty finite families exist.

ideas.what: Equivalence between ateliers with a family of figures and abstract data (M, ≤, ≪, ∥) satisfying axioms M0–M4, corresponding to At1–7, AtL1–3, AtCL(open)
ideas.modern_name: Order-theoretic / incidence-geometric reconstruction of a geometry from its poset of figures (cf. synthetic and convex geometry axiomatics, face posets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Various authors (Pasch–Hilbert axiomatics; convexity spaces; abstract polytopes)
ideas.where_published: Unpublished 'Analysis situs' / 'Géométrie formelle' manuscripts (Montpellier archive, cotes 156ff)

ideas.what: Axiom ML6: parallelism of figures defined elementwise from parallelism of elements of L
ideas.modern_name: Induced relation on subsets (relation lifted to the powerset by universal quantification)

ideas.what: Polyhedral ordered set: any two elements with a common upper and lower bound have a meet; equivalently, closed intervals are (meet-)lattices
ideas.modern_name: Poset whose closed intervals are lattices (face posets of polyhedral/regular cell complexes; 'locally lattice' posets, abstract polytopes, intersection property of polyhedral complexes)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Combinatorial topology / polytope theory (e.g. Björner, McMullen–Schulte for abstract polytopes)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an axiomatic 'atelier' theory with open and polyhedral variants, and aims at an abstract characterization of polyhedral geometries via posets of figures with incidence and a parallelism/separation relation. The program is part of the largely unknown 1986 Analysis situs work on tame topology. To my knowledge it was never developed or compared with o-minimal or abstract-polytope axiomatics.
missed.quote: Variante pour ateliers polyédraux. On conserve la même théorie, sauf qu'on change en conséquence la définition de X ≫ Y (p. 29)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor contribution taken alone. As part of the ateliers program, it is an alternative synthetic foundation for tame or PL geometry that could be compared with o-minimal structures and combinatorial cell-complex axiomatics.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a technical step in an unpublished axiomatics. It contains an elementwise-parallelism axiom and a standard 'intervals are lattices' condition for the polyhedral case. The overall atelier program is little known, but nothing on this page would surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: 'deux éléments Y, Z de M_{≤} [-M-]': in the image, M is struck out with ≤ written above. The intended reading is likely 'de M_{≤X}' (i.e. of X̃).
Before 'admettent un inf', the struck-out word ('admet' in the transcription) is deleted in the image. The intended reading is 'qui sont majorés (par un X) et minorés (par un T) admettent un inf'.
In '(ML 6)', the digit 6 is written heavily, possibly overwriting a 5.
The line '∀x,y∈L, x≪X, y≪Y ⇒ x∥y' is correct per the image.
The marginal insertion reads '(satisfaisant At1–At7, AtL1–AtL3, AtCL(pol))' and is attached to 'ateliers polyédraux'.
